children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by setting up the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you some questions about your child (or children).

**First question: How old is your child?**

The age of the child determines the basic eligibility path:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies automatically (with some conditions)
- **16 to 19**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children you'd like to check eligibility for, please let me know about each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), his eligibility will depend on whether he meets certain education or training requirements. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training status.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (still attending), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last few months), OR
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Could you tell me which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is still in education studying for his A-levels, let me move to the next check to verify the education level.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to verify a few more details about Alex's education:

**Questions about Alex's A-level studies:**

1. **Is it full-time education?** (At least 12 hours per week of supervised study)
2. **Is it funded or arranged by his employer?** (or does he have an agreed future job with an employer who's funding it?)
3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (If yes, additional criteria would apply)

A-levels are typically full-time and not employer-funded, so I expect this should be straightforward, but I need to confirm these details to proceed correctly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's full-time - he's at sixth form college doing his A-levels properly, not some part-time thing. No, it's not funded by any employer - he's just a regular student. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's very clear. Alex is doing full-time A-levels at sixth form college (which is approved non-advanced education), it's not employer-funded, and he's not married. This means his education qualifies under the approved education criteria.

Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

For young people aged 16-19 in education, they can still qualify for Child Benefit as long as they're not working 24 hours or more per week.

Does Alex work, and if so, how many hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does have a part-time job - he works at the local supermarket. To be honest, it's actually quite a lot of hours... he works full-time there, so it's more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for being honest about that. This is an important detail. Let me navigate to see what this means for Alex's eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this may be disappointing news, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Even though Alex is still studying for his A-levels (which is approved education), the Child Benefit rules state that a young person aged 16 or over who is working 24 or more hours per week is not considered a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

**Important points:**

- The fact that Alex is working full-time at the supermarket (more than 24 hours per week) means he doesn't qualify, even though he's still in education
- This rule applies to anyone aged 16 or over who works 24+ hours per week

**What happens if circumstances change:**

If Alex's working hours reduce to less than 24 hours per week while he continues his A-level studies, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to inform HMRC of the change in circumstances.

**Do you have any questions about this decision, or is there anything else I can help clarify?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's a shame, but I understand. Just to be clear though - even though he's still doing his A-levels full-time, because he's also working full-time at the supermarket, that means he doesn't qualify?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. I can see why this might seem a bit counterintuitive, so let me clarify:

**The situation:**
- Alex is doing full-time A-levels ✓ (which is approved education)
- BUT he's also working 24+ hours per week at the supermarket ✗

**The rule:**
For young people aged 16-19, even if they're in approved education like A-levels, if they're working 24 or more hours per week in paid employment, they are not considered a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

The policy reasoning is that a young person working full-time hours (24+ per week) is considered to be sufficiently independent and earning their own income, even if they're also studying.

**To qualify, Alex would need to:**
- Continue his full-time A-levels education, AND
- Work less than 24 hours per week (or not work at all)

So if his supermarket hours were to reduce to part-time (under 24 hours per week) while he's still doing his A-levels, then he would qualify again and you could reclaim Child Benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like me to explain about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that makes sense now. Thanks for explaining it so clearly. I appreciate your help, even though it's not the answer I was hoping for!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I know it's not the outcome you were hoping for, but I'm glad I could explain it clearly for you.

Just to summarize and formally record this assessment, let me document the decision:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Remember:** If Alex's work situation changes and his hours drop below 24 per week while he's still studying, you can contact HMRC to reclaim Child Benefit. It's worth keeping that in mind!

If you have any other questions in the future or if circumstances change, feel free to reach out. Best of luck to Alex with his A-levels! 📚
